_comment: The authoritative sources the AI Business Intelligence engine is allowed to lean on. Two kinds, and the difference matters: `machine` sources have a documented API or bulk download, so their numbers are ingested and injected into the model as ground truth. `portal` sources are human-facing databases with no stable public API — they are never scraped and never paraphrased as fact; they are surfaced as verification links so a founder can check a claim at the source. countryUrlStatus is deliberately conservative: `verified` means the pattern is documented and stable, `unverified` means it is believed correct and degrades to a valid landing page if it drifts, `none` means only the index is offered and the user filters by country themselves. Never promote a status without actually opening the resulting URL.

sources.name: Worldwide Governance Indicators
sources.use: Governance quality of the jurisdiction: rule of law, corruption control, regulatory quality. Shapes risk sections and how strongly the compliance stage insists on local verification.

sources.name: World Development Indicators
sources.use: Macro context for financial assumptions: GDP per capita, inflation, population, internet and mobile penetration, access to electricity, domestic credit to the private sector.

sources.name: Business Ready (B-READY)
sources.use: Successor to Doing Business. Scores the regulatory framework, public services and operational efficiency of starting and running a firm. Published as bulk files rather than an API, so it is ingested from the data catalogue download, not fetched live.
sources.note: No public per-country API. The ingestion script reads the downloaded dataset; until the founder runs it, B-READY contributes nothing rather than being guessed at.

sources.name: Human Development Report — Data Center
sources.use: Human development context: HDI, inequality, gender inequality, schooling and life expectancy. Keeps market sizing honest about purchasing power and human capital.
sources.note: The API requires a free key (HDR_API_KEY). Without it the source contributes links only.

sources.name: Investment Policy Hub — investment laws
sources.license: Consult the portal's terms before redistributing
sources.use: National investment laws, investment treaties and policy measures. The reference a founder checks for foreign-ownership rules, incentives and investor protections.
sources.note: Country pages are keyed by internal numeric ids, not ISO codes, so no deep link can be derived safely. The checklist links the index and names the country to filter on.

sources.name: WIPO Lex
sources.license: Consult the portal's terms before redistributing
sources.attribution: World Intellectual Property Organization, WIPO Lex
sources.use: National intellectual-property laws and treaties. The source for trademark, patent and copyright obligations behind any 'protect the brand' item.

sources.name: NATLEX
sources.license: Consult the portal's terms before redistributing
sources.attribution: ILO, NATLEX database of national labour legislation
sources.use: National labour, social security and human-rights legislation. Backs every employment item in the regulatory checklist.

sources.name: Universal Human Rights Index
sources.license: Consult the portal's terms before redistributing
sources.attribution: UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights
sources.use: Human-rights recommendations issued to each country. Relevant to responsible-business and ESG sections, and to sectors touching labour, land or vulnerable groups.

sources.name: United Nations Treaty Collection
sources.license: Consult the portal's terms before redistributing
sources.use: Status of ratification of multilateral treaties — trade, arbitration, environment, labour. Tells a founder which international regimes bind their jurisdiction.
sources.note: Recorded here as the collection's root. The link originally supplied pointed at the portal's own PageNotFound error page and would have shipped a dead link into every dossier.
